title: A Reddit user's RTX 5080 died after installing unofficial DLSS 5 in GTA 5
excerpt: One user's mod fueled experiment with unofficial DLSS and ReoDx ended in sudden failure and an expensive lesson.
content_html:
Published Sep 21, 2026, 10:47 AM EDT

Sara Heritage is a tech and gaming journalist, who's currently making her way up to Master Ball rank in Pokemon Champions. Bylines in IGN, GAMINGbible, The Gamer and more. You can usually find her tinkering with tech, or restoring old consoles, always with one of her 3 cats nearby. Come and talk with her over on Twitter @SHeritageJourno.

A Reddit user claims that an unofficial version of DLSS 5 in a heavily modified session of Grand Theft Auto 5 damaged their brand-new high-end graphics card.

What is DLSS 5?

This user's adventures in Los Santos came to a sorry end

For those not in the know, DLSS 5, or Deep Learning Super Sampling version 5, is NVIDIA's latest AI-powered image upscaling technology you can use if you've got a compatible GeForce graphics cards. It uses AI to generate high-quality frames from lower-resolution inputs, which basically means you get 'better' visuals and improved performance in supported games. It's a bit of a controversial topic, with some people not a fan of how it makes games look.

But one DLSS 5 fan, a Reddit user, waited six years to move to a high-end system based on an RTX 5080, and it ended in disaster. The user claims the GPU failed just one month after they got the system. They claim the system worked well under heavy graphical loads, including ray tracing and frame generation in more recent games, but they ran into a few problems soon after the user tried an unofficial version of DLSS 5.0.1, which they obtained from a community source, and inserted it into Grand Theft Auto 5 by using the ReoDx wrapper. This involved manually replacing the game's original DLSS DLL file in the GTA 5 folder and using ReoDx's configuration tool to force compatibility, together with several active visual mods, including the LSPDFR police modification.

On day two of testing the setup, the user experienced a sudden system freeze with intense screen flashing, which was apparently impossible to recover. When the system was restarted, it failed to power up and displayed a black screen with no response from the keyboard or any other peripherals. Only after diagnostic tests were carried out was it found that the system could boot by removing the graphics card and using the integrated graphics, whereas putting the RTX 5080 back in caused the system to fail again.

It’s, well, not a happy ending, but the user did eventually get a replacement GPU and learned a very expensive lesson — don’t mess around with unofficial software injections unless you know what you’re doing.

Now, let me be clear: there’s no proof the software caused the issue. In fact, the majority on voices on the thread suggest it’s probably either a coincidence or pre-existing instability of the hardware. Third-party DLSS versions and lots of mods can significantly increase GPU workload (higher sustained utilisation, ray tracing, or neural-rendering work), which can push a card into higher boost/power states. That extra stress might reveal pre‑existing hardware defects or cause failures on faulty cards.

If you’re interested in modding, make sure you trust the mod you're installing. Community repositories such as Nexus Mods have moderation and user feedback systems that reduce—but do not eliminate—risks. Always review comments, use trusted authors, and take safety precautions when installing community content.

I bet GTA V looked great while it ran, though.

​
